name: Adamorobe Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Village sign language (Ghana); word stress category not applicable; Nyst 2007 dissertation describes it but no spoken-stress statement possible.

sources.citation: Nyst, Victoria. 2007. A descriptive analysis of Adamorobe Sign Language (Ghana). PhD dissertation, Universiteit van Amsterdam. Utrecht: LOT (LOT Dissertation Series 151). 245 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing at sign/word level. Ch. 2 'Phonology' (pp. 47-87) covers only non-hand articulators, phonetic and phonemic handshapes and iconic motivation of handshapes; no section on movement, syllable, prosody or stress. Full-text search for stress/prosod/accent/prominen/emphas gives no sign-level statement. Only prosody remarks are clause-level: verb sequences 'form a prosodic unit' with a consistent pattern of eye gaze and handedness and fluid transitions (pp. 179-181, 189, 191); clause boundaries marked by the sign FINISH or re-established eye contact/head nod (§1.8.3.1, pp. 42-43).
